title: Enforceable model reference resolution and fallback contract for SDK/API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a single, implementable contract for how the Redwood API and SDK resolve a model reference supplied by a customer. The contract must cover three common reference forms (mutable tag, semver range, immutable commit/hash), specify deterministic resolution order and fallbacks, define observable resolution traces, and require that any resolved model has an associated published performance profile. The outcome will reduce customer confusion, make rollouts predictable, and enable clear migration tooling.
rationale: Customers currently use a mix of tags, semver-like names, and commit hashes when onboarding open models. Without a standardized resolution contract SDK behavior differs across releases and edge cases cause silent fallback to incompatible model variants. This leads to unexpected latency/cost changes and makes debugging regressions hard. We need a developer-facing contract that is explicit and enforceable by both the API and the SDKs.
proposal_summary: Introduce a deterministic resolver with explicit precedence: (1) exact immutable reference (commit/hash or exact version string) -> resolve only exact match; (2) semver range -> match latest compatible stable release within range; (3) tag reference -> resolve to latest tag target but require optional 'stability' flag if used in production; (4) user-provided fallback list -> attempt each sequentially. SDKs will expose resolution_trace in responses and surface clear error types (ResolutionError, AmbiguousReferenceError, PerformanceProfileMissing). The control plane must validate that every resolved version has a performance profile v1 published and pass quality gates before returning it to production routes.
api_changes:
- Add /resolve-model endpoint (internal) to return resolved_model_id and resolution_trace.
- Augment generation API response header X-Redwood-Resolved-Model with resolved_model_ref and profile_id.
- New error codes: 409: AmbiguousReference, 424: ProfileNotPublished, 422: InvalidSemverRange.
- SDK convenience: ModelRef.resolve() and ModelRef.pin() helpers; opt-in 'strict' mode to reject mutable tag resolution.
sdk_behaviour:
- Default: SDK will attempt resolution with fallback policy and include resolution_trace in debug logs.
- Strict mode: throw ResolutionError if provided reference is mutable tag or semver range and resolves to non-exact version.
- Caching: SDK-level memoization TTL 5 minutes; respect server cache-control header.
- Telemetry: emit resolved_model_id and resolution_path event for every first request after cache miss.
performance_profile_contract:
- Every model version (resolved_model_id) must have a linked performance_profile_id.
- Performance profile metadata includes: latency_p50/95, throughput_baseline, memory_footprint, supported_sequence_lengths, quantization_recommendation.
- Control plane validation: block resolution to model versions lacking a published profile for the target deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Console: expose model-version -> profile mapping and a regression alert when profile metrics change >15% vs published baseline.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs and API return deterministic resolution_trace for the following inputs: exact-hash, exact-version, semver ranges (>=1.2.0 <2.0.0), tag names (e.g., 'stable', 'experiment'), and fallback-lists.
Strict mode rejects mutable tags in unit/integration test harness with clear error codes.
Control plane rejects publishing of a model_version if no performance_profile exists for the target deployment class.
Telemetry events produced for resolution decisions and surfaced in console logs and per-route cost/latency breakdowns.
E2E tests validate fallback order and that a resolved model with missing profile returns 424 with remediation guidance.
Docs updated: API reference, SDK migration guide, and a public 'model-resolution' runbook linked from the Console.
migration_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Implement resolver in control plane and SDK opt-in strict mode; add resolution_trace.
- Phase 2: Enforce profile presence for new model versions and add API error codes.
- Phase 3: Default strict mode enabled for production tenants after 4 weeks of telemetry show <0.1% failures.
- Provide automated migrations: tag-to-commit helper that snapshots current tag target into a stable version and publishes missing performance profile via CI job.
open_questions: Should semver pre-release labels (e.g., 1.2.3-beta.1) be considered for semver ranges by default?
What is the expected TTL for server-side resolution caches in Dedicated vs Hosted?
Do we allow a user-specified 'grace_period' where tag resolution will still succeed even if profile is missing (for quick internal testing)?
security_considerations: Model refs and trace data may expose internal model IDs — ensure resolution_trace respects tenant isolation and redacts any org-internal IDs in console views for non-admin users. Audit logs must record resolution decisions and who initiated the model onboarding/publish action.
rollout_notes: Start with SDKs shipping opt-in API and a 'resolution_trace' debug flag. Monitor Console alerts for PerformanceProfileMissing and AmbiguousReference spikes. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to contact any tenants using mutable tags in production before flipping strict mode.
